headline: A drone attack has shut down a third Yandex data centre in four days, this time in Russia's Vladimir region.
score_reason: Kept at 7: the company and two news agencies agree, a third site is down with outages in several countries, but the damage and restart time are not known.
importance_line: Users of Yandex's taxi, banking and other services in dozens of Russian cities and three neighbouring countries lose access, and data centres are becoming repeated targets in the war, but the lasting damage and any restart date are not known.
summary: Reuters reports, as carried by Devdiscourse, that Yandex, the Russian technology and AI company often called Russia's Google, says a drone attack damaged its data centre in the Vladimir region and shut it down completely, with some services unavailable and no one hurt. New since our 10 Oct edition, which carried the BBC on the Sasovo and Kaluga strikes, this is the third Yandex site hit in four days; the Associated Press calls the attack Ukrainian and, citing the Russian outlet Astra, says users in dozens of Russian cities, Kazakhstan, Belarus and Armenia could not order taxis or reach banking services.
notes: Read Reuters text via Devdiscourse (Reuters page blocked) and AP via ABC News. Vladimir strike itself is today's event; marked follow-up of the 10 Oct item as the pool flags. machine_action false: the story is the outage, not a machine shown working.
